Theme

# Philosophy quotes about justice

Justice concerns fairness, rights, desert, and the arrangement of institutions that claim to treat people as equals.

19 passages · 8+ thinkers in this selection

## Why this theme matters

Distributive, retributive, and restorative justice name different problems. Political philosophy asks what a just society owes its members and outsiders.

## In the history of philosophy

Plato’s Republic, Confucian rightful rule, social-contract theories, and contemporary egalitarian debates structure the field.

## Thinkers in this collection

[Socrates](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/socrates) , [Plato](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/plato) , [Mencius](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/mencius) , [John Locke](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/john-locke) , [Wang Yangming](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/wang-yangming) , [Epicurus](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/epicurus) , [Simone de Beauvoir](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/simone-de-beauvoir) , [Elizabeth Anscombe](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/elizabeth-anscombe)

## Frequently asked questions

### What is justice in philosophy?

It is the virtue and institutional standard of giving each their due—though “due” is endlessly debated.

### What are the types of justice?

Common distinctions include distributive, procedural, retributive, and restorative justice.
